belief: I won’t know my loved ones after the resurrection.
meta: A Christian look at the fear that you won’t know your loved ones after the resurrection, with Scripture, questions, and homework for finding hope in the truth.
origins: Grief over someone you deeply miss. Hearing that in heaven we will be so focused on God that we won’t know anyone. Jesus’ words that there is no marriage in the resurrection, which can feel like a loss of relationship. Vague ideas about heaven. Fear that your love will be lost.
teaches: Scripture gives us strong reasons for hope. Paul comforted grieving believers that God will bring with Jesus those who have died, and that we will be together with them and with the Lord. Moses and Elijah were recognized at the transfiguration. The disciples recognized the risen Jesus. David said of his child who died, “I will go to him.” We will know fully, even as we are fully known. Relationships will be made perfect, not erased.
self_statements: I’ll never see my loved one again.
Our relationship will be gone in heaven.
Heaven will feel lonely without them.
My love for them won’t matter anymore.
errors: Predicting loss of relationship without Scripture saying so.
Focusing on unknowns while overlooking promises of reunion.
Taking “no marriage in the resurrection” to mean no relationships at all.
Letting pain shape your picture of eternity.
questions: What does Paul say about being together with those who died in Christ?
Did the disciples recognize the risen Jesus?
What did David expect about his child?
Will I know less or more fully in heaven?
Could relationships be made better rather than erased?
How does this hope help me grieve today?
truth: I have good reason to hope I will know my loved ones in Christ after the resurrection. God will bring them with Jesus, and we will be together with the Lord forever. I will know fully, even as I am fully known. Our relationships will be made perfect, not erased. I can grieve with hope.
hw_questions: What does Paul say about being together?
What did David expect about his child?
Will I know less or more fully?
How does this hope help me grieve?
hw_truths: We will be together with the Lord forever.
God will bring with Jesus those who died in Him.
I will know fully, even as I am fully known.
Relationships will be made perfect, not erased.
Love in Christ is not lost.
log: Each day, write one thing I look forward to sharing with my loved one in God’s presence.
name_example: Sarah, we do not want you to be uninformed about those who sleep in death, so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.
actions: Read 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 each night this week,
and underline every word of hope.
Write a letter to your loved one
about what you look forward to when you see them again.
and notice how the disciples recognized the risen Jesus.
with someone who also loved them.
prayer: Father, thank You for the people I love who have died in Christ. Help me reject the fear that I won’t know them after the resurrection. Thank You that we will be together with the Lord forever, knowing fully as we are fully known. Help me grieve with hope. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Christ’s resurrection and forgiveness provide hope beyond sin and death.
Christian hope looks toward resurrection, restored life, and worship with God.
Jesus is present in suffering and is greater than the circumstances we face.
Larry Ford and Lillie Knauls with Gaither
